info.title: Carrier Erase
info.description: Three notch filters sit at 15.5, 17.5 and 19.5 kHz, where stationary tonal peaks are often measured. This knob sets how wide each notch is.
info.howItWorks: Three cascaded biquad notch filters at 15500, 17500 and 19500 Hz. Higher values widen each notch (Q falls from 28.0 to 2.5, 24.0 to 2.5, and 20.0 to 2.0), covering a broader band around each centre frequency.
info.tradeoff: Very high values widen the notches into the top octave and can dull cymbals and air. The Quality Gate limiter still holds the ceiling.

info.title: Stride Remove
info.description: Two narrow peaking cuts in the low mids, at 172.3 Hz and its second harmonic 344.6 Hz, for periodic resonances that show up there in a measurement.
info.howItWorks: Two peaking biquads (Q 6 and Q 7). Depth scales with the knob: up to -10 dB at 172.3 Hz and -7 dB at 344.6 Hz.
info.tradeoff: Higher values remove more energy at those two frequencies but can thin low-mid body if the track has real bass content there.

info.title: Stego Strip
info.purpose: A single peaking cut at 3800 Hz
info.description: One peaking cut in the presence band at 3800 Hz. The cepstral echo reading in the telemetry panel is a measurement only; this control is a fixed-frequency EQ cut.
info.howItWorks: A single peaking biquad at 3800 Hz, Q 3, with depth scaling from 0 dB down to -8 dB.
info.tradeoff: Moderate values leave vocal presence intact; high values soften the 3-4 kHz presence region.

info.title: Neural Scrub
info.purpose: A high-shelf cut whose corner slides from 19 kHz down to 11 kHz
info.description: A high-shelf attenuator for excess energy at the top of the spectrum. Both the corner frequency and the depth follow the knob.
info.howItWorks: One high-shelf biquad. The corner slides from 19 kHz at 0% to 11 kHz at 100%, and the shelf gain runs from 0 dB down to -12 dB. Deshimmer adds up to +20 points of effective strength.
info.tradeoff: Aggressive settings pull the corner into the audible treble and dull cymbals; low settings stay above most musical content.

info.title: Spectral Blend
info.description: Two peaking cuts in the upper mids, aimed at harsh resonant peaks that the analyzer reports above its prominence target.
info.howItWorks: Two peaking biquads at 4200 Hz (Q 2) and 7600 Hz (Q 2.5), scaling from 0 dB down to -6 dB and -7 dB. Deshimmer adds up to +15 points of effective strength.
info.tradeoff: Higher values tame harshness but soften vocal bite and snare crack; the cuts are narrow enough to leave the rest of the band alone.

info.title: Phase Scatter
info.purpose: Three all-pass stages at 850, 2400 and 6800 Hz
info.description: All-pass filters shift phase around three centre frequencies without changing the magnitude response.
info.howItWorks: Three all-pass biquads at 850, 2400 and 6800 Hz. Q scales from 0.5 to 8.0, 0.8 to 8.8, and 1.0 to 9.5, which steepens the phase transition around each centre.
info.tradeoff: Magnitude is untouched, but steep phase shifts can smear transients and shift stereo imaging at high settings.

info.title: Stat Normalize
info.description: A gentle soft-knee waveshaper that rounds off sample peaks, normalized so the curve reaches unity at full scale.
info.howItWorks: A WaveShaperNode with the curve x / (1 + 0.25k|x|), multiplied by (1 + 0.25k) so peak gain stays at unity. k is the knob value / 100, and the node runs at 2x oversampling.
info.tradeoff: Low settings are close to transparent; high settings add mild harmonic colouration and slightly reduce crest factor.

info.title: Hash Break
info.purpose: A slow sine LFO modulating a 3 ms delay
info.description: A very short delay whose length drifts slowly, so the signal is never sample-identical from one moment to the next.
info.howItWorks: A 3 ms DelayNode modulated by a sine oscillator running at 0.25-0.8 Hz. Modulation depth scales from 0.1 ms up to about 1.8 ms.
info.tradeoff: At high depth the slow delay drift becomes audible as a faint chorusing or pitch wobble on sustained tones.

info.title: Room Inject
info.purpose: Two delay taps at 16 ms and 31 ms, mixed back in
info.description: Two short delay taps stand in for early room reflections and are mixed back under the dry signal.
info.howItWorks: A send feeds two parallel delays at 16 ms and 31 ms, both through a 4200 Hz lowpass, then back through a return gain that scales from 0 up to 0.25.
info.tradeoff: Adds a sense of space. High wet mixes thicken the sound and can blur fast transients.

info.title: Texture Inject
info.purpose: Asymmetric tanh saturation with a small even-harmonic term
info.description: A saturating waveshaper that adds low-order harmonics, the way analogue gain stages colour a signal when pushed.
info.howItWorks: A WaveShaperNode with tanh(drive * x) times (1 - 0.05 * amount * x^2), where drive is 1 + 1.5 * amount. The squared term makes the curve asymmetric, adding even harmonics. Runs at 2x oversampling.
info.tradeoff: Adds warmth and presence at low settings; high settings audibly drive and compress peaks.

info.title: Deshimmer
info.purpose: A 10 kHz high-shelf cut plus extra scrub and blend strength
info.description: Reduces metallic shimmer and watery sustain for sound quality. It does not remove watermarks and does not affect AI detection.
info.howItWorks: Gentle HF shelf at 10 kHz (down to -6 dB) plus boosts to neural scrub (+0.20x) and spectral blend (+0.15x), scaled by the measured shimmer score in AUTO.
info.tradeoff: Higher values dull highs; clean tracks stay near 0.

info.title: Bandwidth Heal
info.description: A high-shelf EQ at 12 kHz for the air band. Boost it to open up a dull top end, cut it to pull back excess brightness.
info.howItWorks: One high-shelf biquad at 12000 Hz, Q 0.7. The knob value is applied directly as shelf gain in dB, from -6 to +6.
info.tradeoff: Boosting lifts whatever is already up there, including hiss; it cannot restore content a codec removed above the cutoff.

info.title: Dynamics
info.purpose: A bus compressor with a crest-aware threshold
info.description: Gentle bus compression to tie the mix together. The threshold also accounts for the measured crest factor, so an already-squashed track is compressed less.
info.howItWorks: A DynamicsCompressorNode: ratio 1.5:1 up to 4.0:1, knee 10 dB, attack 25 ms, release 140 ms. Threshold runs from -6 dB down to -24 dB, capped by a crest-derived limit.
info.tradeoff: Higher settings glue the track but reduce transient punch and dynamic range.

info.title: Quality Gate
info.description: Sets the brickwall limiter ceiling: higher level lowers the ceiling for stricter limiting.
info.howItWorks: Maps level 1-6 to a DynamicsCompressor threshold from -0.65 dB down to -2.9 dB, knee 0, ratio 20:1, attack 3 ms, release 50 ms.
info.tradeoff: Lower level = higher ceiling (-0.65 dB), gentler limiting; higher level = lower ceiling (-2.9 dB), stricter limiting.

info.title: Master Output
info.description: The final gain stage, used for monitoring level and for loudness trim when AUTO is not driving the chain.
info.howItWorks: A GainNode set to 10^(dB/20). When AUTO has measured the track's integrated loudness, the chain applies its calibrated trim instead and this knob is held at unity.
info.tradeoff: Use to balance monitoring volume or match pre-processing loudness; the limiter and -1 dB ceiling still apply upstream.
